# TextInput

[Framework](README.md) · `DotGame.Framework.Input` · class

```csharp
public sealed class TextInput : IDisposable
```

A live, framework-owned text-input control backed by the platform's native text editor (browser `<input>`, iOS `UITextField`, Android `EditText`, SDL3 text-input). Created via [`InputService.CreateTextInput`](InputService.md#createtextinput); the handle is registered continuously with the platform so that user gestures (taps on the canvas-projected [`Bounds`](#bounds)) can focus the editor synchronously inside the trusted gesture handler — required by iOS Safari to bring up the soft keyboard.

## Remarks

Mutating [`Bounds`](#bounds), [`Text`](#text), [`InputType`](#inputtype), [`MaxLength`](#maxlength), or [`IsMultiline`](#ismultiline) pushes the new state to the platform editor. Events are raised on the game thread.

## Properties

### Bounds

```csharp
public Rectangle Bounds { get; set; }
```

Types: [`Rectangle`](Rectangle.md)

Position and size of the on-canvas text field in viewport pixels. The platform editor's transparent overlay is positioned to match so that user taps inside this rectangle are captured natively by the browser and focus the editor synchronously (required by iOS Safari to show the soft keyboard).

On non-overlay platforms (iOS/Android/SDL3) the bounds are recorded but the visible representation is drawn by the game. Setting an empty rectangle hides the overlay.

### Composition

```csharp
public string Composition { get; }
```

The text an input method is composing (Japanese or Chinese input, say), not yet part of [`Text`](#text), for a game to show at the end of it; empty when there is none. On Android and iOS, the system's editor keeps composing text in [`Text`](#text) itself, so this stays empty.

### IsMultiline


The most characters it takes, or null for no limit.

## Methods

### Dispose

```csharp
public void Dispose()
```

Releases the platform editor.

### Focus

```csharp
public void Focus()
```

Programmatically gives keyboard focus to the platform editor.

On iOS Safari and Chrome-iOS the soft keyboard only appears when [`Focus`](#focus) is invoked synchronously inside a trusted user-gesture handler (e.g. in response to a tap). When called outside of a gesture (for example from a scene's `OnNavigatedTo`), WebKit moves keyboard focus silently but suppresses the soft keyboard. The WebGL platform detects this and defers raising [`GotFocus`](#gotfocus) until real input is observed (a user gesture, key, or pointer event on the overlay), unless a hardware keyboard is detected via the platform's precision-input media query, in which case focus is confirmed immediately. This matches the behavior documented by Flutter Web, Unity WebGL, Godot Web, Blazor, and MAUI Blazor Hybrid.

A focus request the platform muted is not retried: on the web the user's tap on the field's transparent overlay focuses it natively and raises the soft keyboard, which is the expected mobile interaction.
